name: Dreadmurk Shore
summary: Fog and Mirefin murlocs endanger travelers on Dreadmurk Shore, between Theramore Isle and the Barrens. Sea beasts prowl the water, making this coast a dangerous passage through Dustwallow Marsh.

sections.title: A Treacherous Coast
sections.body: At Dustwallow Marsh’s northeastern edge, muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands lie between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold. The Mirefin tribe holds this coast. These territorial murlocs attack travelers who come near their villages. Sea turtles and other aquatic predators patrol the shallows, while the swamplands bring danger from inland.

sections.title: Defias Infiltrators
sections.body: A Defias Brotherhood ship wrecked between Dreadmurk Shore and Alcaz Island. Outlaws spilled onto the sand and islets. These human criminals came from the Eastern Kingdoms and now lie close to Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s stronghold. Their presence draws Theramore’s attention and threatens the fragile balance of power across the bay.

faq.answer: Dreadmurk Shore runs along Dustwallow Marsh’s northeastern coast, facing the Great Sea between Theramore Isle and the Barrens, near Northwatch Hold.

faq.q: Why are there Defias bandits on this shore?
faq.answer: A Defias Brotherhood ship recently wrecked offshore between Dreadmurk Shore and Alcaz Island. Survivors reached the isolated beach and outcroppings, where they made temporary camps and tried to salvage their sunken cargo.

faq.q: Who are the murlocs living along the beach?
faq.answer: The Mirefin murloc tribe lives along the coast. Its members built crude fishing settlements on the sandbanks and rocky islets, and fiercely guard their territory from Theramore patrols and shipwrecked intruders.

faq.q: Is Dreadmurk Shore controlled by Theramore?
faq.answer: Theramore claims authority over the lands around the island, but Dreadmurk Shore remains lawless. Wild marshy shoals and murloc and brigand inhabitants keep Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s sentries from regular patrols.

angles.text: Defias Brotherhood survivors near Theramore suggest conspiracies reaching beyond Westfall. They threaten Alliance stability in Kalimdor.
As a rogue, you can track clandestine Defias cargo through isolated camps and sunken wreckage. Or you can slip past the violent Mirefin sentinels.
